subject: Private Control Plane: operator access model & SAML/SCIM implementation questions
messages:
From: Acme Security <security@acme-corp.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Cc: federation@globalit.com
Date: Sat, 8 Nov 2025 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Private CP access: operator accounts / SAML & SCIM questions

Hi Vivek,

Thanks for the demo last week. Our security team and platform engineers reviewed the private control plane design and have a few concrete requirements before we sign the security addendum:

- We need SAML-based SSO for operator accounts, with ability to assert role/group attributes.
- SCIM provisioning for operator groups (create/update/delete) mapped to Redwoods operator roles; de-provisioning window must be auditable.
- Clear mapping for two operator tiers: "operator" (deploy/read) and "admin" (deploy/read/write + billing).
- Audit logs of operator actions pushed to our S3+KMS or available via retention policy (we require 13 months).
- Need clarity on session lifetime, whether we support short-lived credentials and enforced MFA for admin role.
- Want an accepted fallback pattern if SCIM provisioning fails (manual onboarding procedure + TTL).

Attached is our SSO configuration dump (ACME_SSO_Config.pdf) showing attribute names. Can you share a proposed mapping and any constraints we should be aware of for VPC/on-prem control plane? Also please list the artifacts we need to exchange for X.509 certs and test users.

Appreciate a short runbook — we are trying to close this week.

Thanks,
Sam Rivera
Security Architect, Acme Corp
security@acme-corp.com

Attachments: ACME_SSO_Config.pdf

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
To: Sam Rivera <security@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 8 Nov 2025 11:20:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Private CP access: operator accounts / SAML & SCIM questions

Sam — thanks for the clear list. High-level reply and attachments included: proposed_scim_mapping.csv + operator-access-decision-log.md.

Short answers up front:
- SAML assertions: we recommend a single attribute (suggested name: redwood_role) containing one of {operator, admin}. We can also accept group-based assertions; mapping is configurable on a per-tenant basis.
- SCIM provisioning: we'll use SCIM v2.0 to sync groups -> operator roles. Deprovisioning will mark user inactive immediately; the control plane will honor the status change and remove active sessions after a configurable grace period (default 24h, configurable to 72h). We'll include a reconciliation job that runs nightly to catch missed deletes.
- Session lifetime & MFA: admin sessions default to 1 hour and require MFA (SAML ACR check or IdP-enforced). Operator sessions default to 4 hours. We support short-lived K8s service tokens for automation if requested.
- Audit logs: Redwood can export operator audit events to your S3 bucket encrypted with your KMS key. Retention policies are configurable up to 24 months.
- Fallback for SCIM failure: we propose a mutual-action plan: allow manual onboarding via a signed provisioning request (ticket + SSO assertion), create a temporary operator account with 72h TTL, and trigger an alert to both parties.

What's attached:
- proposed_scim_mapping.csv — a suggested attribute -> role mapping (column header = Acme attribute names).
- operator-access-decision-log.md — explains the reasoning for role boundaries and the recommended default TTLs and audit retention.

Next steps: can we schedule a 30-minute tech call with your platform team and GlobalIT federation (for cert exchange) on Mon Nov 10 at 10:00 AM PT? If that works, we'll circulate a concise checklist of the exchange artifacts (cert, metadata, test users, S3 bucket ARN + KMS key ARN).

Regards,
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Product — Private Deployments
Redwood Inference
vivek@redwood.com

Attachments: proposed_scim_mapping.csv, operator-access-decision-log.md

From: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>

On Sat, Nov 8, 2025 at 11:20 AM Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com> wrote:
> Sam — thanks for the clear list. High-level reply and attachments included: proposed_scim_mapping.csv + operator-access-decision-log.md.

Quick operational comments (internal):
- Audit retention: confirm that pushing to customer S3 will not include plaintext PII; filter events to operator-level activity only. We'll default to event-level anonymization for 90 days then full events after escalation. Need legal sign-off for 13-month retention.
- SCIM deprovision timing: prefer default 24h session kill + nightly reconciliation; but add a configurable immediate revoke flag for high-risk tenants.
- Certificates: our control plane will accept IdP metadata and a standard X.509 signing cert (RSA2048 or ECDSA P-256). Provide a script to validate metadata during handoff.

I'll prepare the short checklist for the Monday call.

— Laura
Laura Bennett
Director, Product Security
Redwood Inference

1) Meeting confirmed: Mon Nov 10 10:00 AM PT (calendar invite sent) — attendees: Acme platform, GlobalIT federation, Vivek, Laura, Mina, Marcus.

   - S3 bucket ARN and KMS key ARN for audit export (Acme)
   - SCIM service account credentials for one-way provisioning (Acme)
3) Implementation approach agreed: SCIM -> groups -> Redwood operator roles, SAML assertion attribute redwood_role preferred.
4) Action items:

   - Mina: IAC snippets for S3 export + encryption + log retention (due Wed Nov 12).
